paper.title: Sequential Experimental Design for Transductive Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Transductive linear bandits (pure exploration, fixed confidence)
unmapped: Transductive: measurements are taken from a finite set X while the goal is to identify argmax over a separate finite item set Z (generalizes linear BAI X=Z and combinatorial pure exploration)
delta-PAC fixed-confidence identification of z_* = argmax_{z in Z} z^T theta*
settings.definition_quote: Consider known finite collections of $d$-dimensional vectors $\calX\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and $ \calZ\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ , known confidence $\delta\in(0,1)$, and unknown $\theta^{\ast}\in \mathbb{R}^d$. The objective is to identify $z_{\ast} = \argmax_{z\in \calZ} z^{\top}\theta^{\ast}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$ while taking as few measurements in $\mc{X}$ as possible. ... $R_t= X_{t}^{\top}\theta^{\ast} + \eta_t$ where $\eta_t$ is independent, zero-mean, and 1-sub-Gaussian.

settings.name_in_paper: Transductive linear bandits (pure exploration, fixed confidence) (lower bound)
unmapped: Transductive: measurements from finite set X, identification target argmax over separate finite item set Z

symbols.psi_star: min over designs lambda on X of max_{z != z_*} ||z_*-z||^2_{A(lambda)^{-1}} / ((z_*-z)^T theta*)^2

source.label: thm:LowerBound
source.quote: Assume $\eta_t \overset{iid}{\sim} \calN(0,1)$ for all $t$. Then for any $\delta\in (0,1)$, any $\delta$-PAC algorithm must satisfy \E_{\theta^\ast}[\tau] \geq \log(1/2.4\delta)\min_{\lambda\in \simplex_{\calX}}\max_{z\in \calZ\setminus \{z_{\ast}\}} \frac{\|z_{\ast} - z\|^2_{(\sum_{x\in \calX} \lambda_x x x^\top)^{-1}}}{((z_\ast-z)^\top\theta^{\ast})^2}.

results.notes: Algorithm class: all delta-PAC algorithms (recorded as 'other'). Generalizes Soare's linear BAI and combinatorial pure exploration lower bounds.

symbols.gamma_p: free parameter gamma > 0 of the construction; on the instances psi_star <= c'(d + 1/gamma)

conditions: X = Z (linear bandit special case), specific constructed instance family Theta
algorithm takes a static (non-adaptive) allocation and is delta-PAC
for every theta in Theta, psi_star <= c'(d + 1/gamma)

source.label: prop:fixedLowerBound
source.quote: Let $c,c'$ be universal constants. For any $\gamma > 0$, $d$ even, there exists sets $\calX=\calZ \subset \mb{R}^d$ and a set $\Theta \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, such that $\inf_{\mc{A}}\max_{\theta\in \Theta} \E_\theta[\tau] \geq \frac{c d\log(1/\delta)}{\gamma}$ where $\mc{A}$ is the set of all algorithms that are $\delta$-PAC for $\mc{X},\mc{Z}$ and take a static allocation of samples. On the other hand $\psi^{\ast}/c'\leq  d+\frac{1}{\gamma}$ for every choice of $\theta^\ast \in \Theta$.

results.notes: Shows static allocations can be a factor ~d worse than psi_star. Restricted algorithm class (static allocations); worst case over finite instance family.

symbols.rho_t: rho(Y(S_t)) = min_lambda max_{y in Y(S_t)} ||y||^2_{A(lambda)^{-1}}, S_t = {z: Delta(z) <= 2^{-t}}
symbols.r_eps: r(epsilon), minimum number of samples for the rounding procedure (can be O(d/epsilon^2))

tuning: epsilon-efficient rounding procedure with approximation factor eps_alg (default 1/5)

source.label: thm:SampleComplexity
source.quote: With probability greater than $1-\delta$, using an $\epsilon$-efficient rounding procedure, Algorithm~\ref{alg:main} correctly identifies the optimal arm $z_*$ and requires a worst-case sample complexity \[\randnumsamples \leq \sum_{\phaseindex=1}^{\lfloor \log_2(1/\Delta_{\min}) \rfloor} \max\big\{8 \big\lceil (2^{\phaseindex+1})^2 \rho(\yset(\sset_{\phaseindex}))(1+ \epsilon)\log(\phaseindex^2|\calZ|^2/\delta)\big\rceil, r(\epsilon)\big\}\] ...

results.notes: Placement of factor 8 inside/outside the ceiling differs between theorem statement and algorithm; recorded as in the theorem. Algorithm is delta-PAC (correct w.p. >= 1-delta).

symbols.psi_star: lower-bound complexity min_lambda max_{z != z_*} ||z_*-z||^2_{A(lambda)^{-1}} / Delta(z)^2
symbols.r_eps: r(epsilon), rounding procedure minimum sample size, can be O(d/epsilon^2)

source.label: thm:SampleComplexity
source.quote: Furthermore, $N \leq c \psi^{\ast}\log(1/\Delta_{\min})\log(|\calZ|^2\log(1/\Delta_{\min})^2/\delta)+r(\epsilon)\log_2(1/\Delta_{\min})$ for some absolute constant $c$, in other words Algorithm \ref{alg:main} is instance optimal up to logarithmic factors.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit constant 128(1+eps) psi_star log(1/Delta_min) log(log2(1/Delta_min)^2|Z|^2/delta) + (1+r(eps)) log2(1/Delta_min). Matches Theorem 1 up to log factors.
